title: Rotate by k
prompt:
The starter reads a number k, and `ring` in `.data` holds eight words. Rotate `ring` left by k places, in place, before the print loop shows it: rotating `10 20 30 40 50 60 70 80` left by 2 gives `30 40 50 60 70 80 10 20`.

k can be larger than the array. Rotating by 8 puts every element back where it started, so only the remainder of k divided by 8 matters (`udiv` then `msub` gives it). A negative k is an error: print `k must be 0 or more` and return 1 from `main` instead of 0. The number `main` returns becomes the program's exit status, which is how a program tells whatever ran it that something went wrong.

## what is checked

- the line `rotated:` followed by the eight numbers in their new order
- exit status 0, or the error line and exit status 1 for a negative k
- the array is changed in memory (`str` present)
- your program also runs on values of k you do not see: 0, 8, numbers larger than 8, and a negative number
starter:
// rotate an array left by k places, in place
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(base_r, x19)
define(n_r, w20)
define(k_r, w21)
define(i_r, w22)

.data
ring:       .word 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80
n_ring:     .word 8

fmt_in:     .string "%d"
fmt_head:   .string "rotated:"
fmt_el:     .string " %d"
fmt_end:    .string "\n"
msg_bad:    .string "k must be 0 or more\n"

.bss
.align 4
k_m:        .skip 4

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read k
        ldr     x1, =k_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =k_m
        ldr     k_r, [x9]
        ldr     base_r, =ring
        ldr     x9, =n_ring
        ldr     n_r, [x9]

        // TODO: if k is negative, print msg_bad and return 1 from main.
        // Otherwise rotate ring left by k places, in place: the element
        // at index k moves to index 0, and the first k elements wrap
        // around to the end. k can be larger than n.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_head               // print ring as it now sits in memory
        bl      printf
        mov     i_r, 0
        b       show_test
show_loop:
        ldr     x0, =fmt_el
        ldr     w1, [base_r, i_r, sxtw 2]
        bl      printf
        add     i_r, i_r, 1
show_test:
        cmp     i_r, n_r
        b.lt    show_loop
        ldr     x0, =fmt_end
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
